cohort: 124 pregnant women at a medical center in Alabama
finding: Significantly lower breastfeeding intention and prenatal breastfeeding self-efficacy scores were found among Black women, those with a high school education or less, single women, and those who had no breastfeeding experience.
mod_finding: The study found that planned mode of delivery was a significant factor in breastfeeding intention and self-efficacy scores, with lower scores among those planning a Cesarean delivery.
